title: Appwrite
intro: Open-source backend with auth and databases, for developers and the coding agents they build with.
body: Supabase Pro starts at $25 a month. According to the README, Appwrite runs as a managed cloud or self-hosted on your own infrastructure, and the self-hosted route is where the money is saved. Then the server is yours and the upgrades are yours, and when it breaks there's nobody to call. The project has been around a long time and 556 people have contributed. Last commit was today. It got 52 stars today, and a normal day is about 21.
verdict: If you're fine running Docker on your own server, you can cancel Supabase.
other_side: Keep paying if you want someone else to deal with the backend when it goes down.

title: OpenCode
intro: An open source AI coding agent, and you can run it in the terminal or install it as a desktop app.
body:
OpenCode is from the team behind sst. 1,097 people have contributed to it and the last commit was today.

It installs with one command. There's also a desktop app, but that's still in beta.

Claude Code Pro is $20 a month. Paid yearly it comes down to $17. With OpenCode you run it and keep it updated yourself, and the README excerpt doesn't say which model it talks to or what that model costs.
verdict: Run OpenCode next to Claude Code before you cancel anything, and drop the subscription once you've seen what the model bill actually comes to.
other_side: Keep paying if you want someone else to look after the tool and pick up when it breaks.

facts.price_quote: $17 Per month with annual subscription discount ( $200 billed up front). $20 if billed monthly.

title: AutoClip
intro: An open-source desktop app that cuts long videos into short clips, for people who post on TikTok and Douyin.
body: Opus Clip Starter costs $15 a month. AutoClip is free on GitHub, and you paste a link and it renders the clip on your own computer. It still calls cloud models, and the README says those are billed by use. It picked up 983 stars today, a lot more than it usually gets.
verdict: Run AutoClip alongside Opus Clip for a few weeks, and cancel only after that.
other_side: Keep paying if you want one fixed bill and someone to call when it breaks.

title: FreeVideo
intro: An app that runs the MiniMax H3 video model on your own computer, for people making AI videos.
body: Runway Standard is $12 a month if you pay for the year. FreeVideo makes AI videos on your own computer, and the README says 8 GB of VRAM is enough. So you need a graphics card like that, and you run it yourself, and when it breaks there's nobody to call. It got 39 forks today. On a normal day it's around 7. Last commit was yesterday.
verdict: If you have a good graphics card, try FreeVideo next to Runway.
other_side: Keep paying if there's no strong graphics card on your desk or you don't want to run anything yourself.
